messages:
ana: Heads-up — the PTQ canary (v2-liteq) started showing weird funcall parse failures on structured outputs.
max: saw that in telemetry. Parsing errors spike when sigils like `\\u0007` or stray backslashes appear in tool args.
rahul: are these nonprintables coming from the tokenizer or some postprocess?
marta: hypothesis: quantization altered tokenization alignment for some prefix tokens, causing an extra `\\` to be emitted before a closing quote in some runs. low-prob but visible in tail.
nana: (typo) ana: ^ marta nailed it — reproducer: send prompt with long JSON array + kv-prefix, run on canary PTQ vs fp16; PTQ sometimes emits `\\n\\u0000` sequences in middle of strings.
max: example from canary logs: ````
{"tool":"lookup","args":"{\"id\": \"user\\\\\"123\"}"}
````
max: note the triple-escaped quote and then a trailing backslash. parser chokes and our retry logic kicks in.
rahul: And retry logic does what? double-invoke tools?
marta: current retry budget replays the full LLM output through the parser, which can cause duplicate tool calls if downstream code isn't idempotent. We saw 2x billing in a few samples.
ops-bot: incident-alert: 3 duplicate tool invocations detected in production namespace for customer: acme-inc — elevated to eng-ml.
nana: (again typo) ana: For immediate mitigation: can we add a post-LLM sanitize step that strips non-printable control chars (U+0000..U+001F) and normalizes repeated backslashes before parsing? cheap fix for canary.
max: +1. Also add a fast heuristic: if parsed JSON contains identical tool invocation repeated within same response, drop duplicates (idempotency gate).
rahul: long-term: need to pin tokenizer/decoder behavior for PTQ builds. If quantization shifts byte-to-token boundaries, we should run a golden-token alignment test during onboarding.
marta: Agreed. Proposed tasks: 1) short-term sanitizer hook in parser (ana, max) 2) idempotency filter in tool dispatcher (rahul) 3) tokenizer alignment suite added to PTQ CI (marta) 4) replay-run the canary request set to verify no regressions (ops-bot + ci-bot).
ci-bot: CI job queued: `ptq-token-align-check` against v2-liteq canary set — ETA ~45m.
nana: (still typo) ana: I'll push sanitizer PR to staging, include a toggle so we can flip off if it masks real regressions.
max: can you include the exact blacklist regex (control chars + lone backslash before `\"`)? also log sanitized diffs to S3 for inspection.
nana: (fixed) ana: will do. regex: `/[\u0000-\u001F]|\\(?=\")/g` ; will redact payloads and store diffs in `s3://redwood-canary-sanitized-diffs/1779012345/`.
rahul: For the tokenizer suite, we'll add an assert to fail any PTQ build that increases parse-error-rate on the golden set by >0.2% relative to baseline.
marta: also add a small sampling job in production that runs the sanitizer but records original+sanitized parse result for 1% of requests — helps detect if sanitizer hides model regressions.
ops-bot: noted. scheduling the sampling rollout to 1% canary now.
max: thanks. once sanitizer PR is up ping #eng-infra for a quick canary deploy.
nana: (ha) ana: pinged. will link PR here when ready. :pray:
ci-bot: build passed for ptq-token-align-check (sha: d4f3a7) — baseline vs v2-liteq diff coming in 10m.
marta: good thread. follow-ups: create a short postmortem if we see customer-visible duplicates. otherwise mark as canary incident.
nana: (final) ana: PR is up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4821 — includes sanitizer + toggle + logging. please review.
max: reviewing now.
rahul: I'll start the tokenizer alignment harness plan doc in confluence and link back.
ops-bot: incident-alert cleared from prod namespace (duplicates stopped after 1% sampling + sanitizer canary).
marta: closing loop: next steps tracked in the canary epic `E-ptq-parse-robustness`.
